violations.why: Acorn has equal priority and can preempt ridge between its write and read, so the check can see a different value.
Acorn is running fn_cobalt when ridge preempts it and reads v_harbor. Ridge sees the intermediate value 0.
Ridge preempts acorn between its write and the fn_bluff reset, and reads the intermediate value.
Acorn has higher priority and can write v_velvet between ridge's two reads. The reads can then see different values.
Acorn can preempt north in its loop and overwrite v_quill[9000]. North then reads a value it did not write.
Acorn can preempt ridge between its write of v_wharf and the read in fn_cobalt, and write it in between.
